title: North Adams launches senior housing initiative to create innovative solutions for residents 55+ - NewsBreak
text: NORTH ADAMS, Mass. (WWLP) – A new initiative in North Adams aims to tackle the city’s growing need for senior housing by harnessing creativity and community collaboration. The North Adams Partnership has received a competitive grant from AARP to launch an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Design Challenge, focused on creating innovative housing solutions for residents aged 55 and older. The initiative comes at a time when more than 38% of North Adams’ population is over the age of 55, and with much of the city’s housing stock dating back to before 1940, options for older homeowners looking to downsize without leaving their neighborhoods are limited. The ADU Design Challenge invites students, designers, builders, and creative professionals to submit small, efficient, and code-compliant ADU concepts that address the unique needs of older residents. With recent changes to state housing law under the Massachusetts Affordable Homes Act allowing ADUs by-right on single-family zoned properties, the challenge seeks to lower the barriers to construction and empower homeowners to age in place. Design proposals will be evaluated by a panel of residents aged 55 and older, in collaboration with city officials. The top three winning designs will receive commissions and be released as open-source plans, freely available to the public to encourage widespread use. “With the support of AARP, we are exploring housing solutions that are not only senior-friendly, but community-driven,” said Jenny Wright, Executive Director of the North Adams Partnership. “This project elevates the voices and talents of our older residents while directly addressing the housing shortage impacting this very population.” The program also leverages the skills of North Adams’ older adults, many of whom bring decades of professional experience in fields such as healthcare, education, planning, and public service. These volunteers will help promote the challenge, engage with local officials, and support outreach at community events. “I’m so excited to be part of this ADU design challenge—this is exactly the kind of creative, community-powered effort we need right now,” said Alice Bojanowski, a retired city planner and North Adams resident. “Our older residents deserve options that let us stay connected and independent.” Organizers view the initiative as a replicable model for other small cities across Massachusetts and the nation. By combining policy change with grassroots participation, the North Adams ADU Design Challenge aims to build a more inclusive, resilient, and age-friendly community—one innovative design at a time.
